text:
deploy-bot: Starting deploy 2026.03.18-db-backfill with migration id 2026-03-db-017. Rolling window: 02:00-06:00 UTC. Lock risk: short exclusive lock on `user_profiles` schema change.

matt: FYI this backfill updates `preferred_name` from legacy `display_name` for ~18M rows. Backfill will run in batches, uses new `backfill_worker` service.

sara: Are we pinning runtime to v2.3.1 for the migration? We had a regression in v2.4.0 with large transactions.

matt: yes — pin v2.3.1 for the duration. I pushed a release note in the deploy checklist.

jamie: quick summary of escape hatches: 1) abort backfill via deploybot 2) enable row-level throttle 3) fast rollback that reverts schema change (requires downtime).

rachael: what's the rollback criteria? CPU > 85% on primary for >5m? or lock wait > 5000ms?

matt: Proposed thresholds: DB lock wait spike > 2000ms sustained for 2 consecutive 1m windows AND backfill TPS drops >30%. OR error rate on API path hitting user_profile reads >1% (5m window). If met, hit abort and notify oncall.

oncall-bot: @oncall paging rule enabled for error_rate > 1% and db_lock_wait > 2000ms. Pager: @oncall-sre.

devops: Deploybot preflight checklist done. Canary started against 5% traffic for 20m. No schema locks during canary. Telemetry looks ok so far.

matt: Canary results: backfill worker steady at 120rps, avg latency +10ms, no lock waits. Rolling to 25% now.

sara: Reminder: update release notes to mention data-migration ttl and that the feature flag `use_preferred_name` will be off for 24h post-deploy.

jamie: Adding the throttling command here in case we need it: 
```
# throttle backfill to 20rps per worker
deploybot throttle backfill-worker --rate 20 --deployment 2026-03-db-017
```

rachael: Also keep this SQL ready if we need to stop quickly (safe, idempotent):
```
-- make migration reversible: mark remaining rows as pending and flip flag
BEGIN;
UPDATE migrations.meta SET status='paused' WHERE id='2026-03-db-017';
COMMIT;
```

matt: Good. Ops plan: 02:00 UTC start, canary 5->25->60->100 over ~90m with checks at each step. If any gate fails, abort and roll to pinned v2.3.1.

devops: Note on pinned runtime: runbook updated at https://intra.redwood/ops/runbooks/db-backfill-2026-03 (link).

oncall-bot: Deploybot logged action: canary -> 25% at 3290012460 by deploy-bot.

matt: Metrics to watch in the first 30m: lock_wait_99, db_cpu, p99_api_latency, backfill_rows_processed/s, error_rate_user_profile. Alerts wired to #incidents and pager.

sara: I'm on standby for hotfix if we see p99 API latency > 500ms.

jamie: Also coordinate with support — put a banner template just in case we need to announce degraded profile search: `Heads up: We're rolling out a profile data migration, you may see intermittent profile name issues for up to 2 hours.`

rachael: One more thing: if we abort after 60% rollout, we need to run a reconciliation job before reattempt. Add to checklist.

matt: Added reconciliation step to release notes and release checklist.

devops: Deploybot: proceed to 60% now. Logging timestamps.

deploy-bot: Proceeding -> 60% at 3290012600. Canary health: ok.

matt: Observability snapshot at 60%: lock_wait_95=120ms, db_cpu=68%, backfill_rps=105, api_p99=120ms. All green. Proceeding to 100%.

rachael: Pushed release notes update to docs site and added rollback instructions.

oncall-bot: Deploy complete at 3290012750. Post-deploy jobs (reconciliation) scheduled at +2h.

matt: Thanks team. Stand down unless pager fires. I'll follow up with final release notes and a short postmortem in #eng-releases tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
